name: Casey Kennington
title: Associate Professor; Boise State Foundation Board Endowed Professor of Computer Science
fitReason: Strong physically grounded human–AI methods overlap: compact language/affect models, online human feedback, incremental dialogue infrastructure and robot behavior generation. Especially relevant to a focused conversational-robot adaptation study rather than dexterous manipulation.

physicalEvidence.summary: August 2026 SIGDIAL paper deploys Retico, a LoRA-adapted DeBERTa-v3-base emotion policy, online GRPO and GRED behavior generation on an actual Cozmo. Its physical outputs include facial/sound displays and drive/head/lift motions. One tutor provided 542 live feedback interactions; the resulting model was evaluated with ten additional participants. This is expressed behavior, not evidence that the robot experiences emotions. The authors explicitly acknowledge single-tutor learning, small evaluation size and synthetic-to-real versus personalization confounding.

shortVisit.summary: The official SLIM contact page gives an email and asks prospective graduate students to explain concrete research fit and contributions. Neither that page nor the current faculty homepage explicitly offers external short-term visits or summer2027 positions.

scoreReasons.fit: 38/40: concrete neural dialogue, interactive RL and physically embodied HRI; narrower than manipulation-oriented foundation models.
scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: directly documented 2026 real Cozmo deployment and human study at current institution.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 0/20: public graduate-contact route does not establish summer or visiting positions.
